moat_against: No passenger switching costs — discretionary, price-compared purchase
Royal Caribbean premium position and MSC Caribbean expansion pressure pricing
Fuel unhedged — small fuel moves swing profit materially
High leverage and heavy recurring capex claim cash before equity holders
Emissions/environmental regulation raises compliance capex on older tonnage
moat_for: Largest global fleet and share (about 40%) across nine brands from value to luxury
Scale purchasing, deployment flexibility, and home-port network
Private destinations (Celebration Key) capture full shore-side spend
Record forward bookings and customer deposits (about $7.6B) give visibility and float
Brand breadth lets Carnival shift ships and pricing tiers by region and segment
moat_justification: Largest global fleet and share across nine brands, scale purchasing, private destinations and a record forward deposit float, but no passenger switching costs, intense rivalry from Royal Caribbean/MSC/Norwegian, unhedged fuel, and a levered capital-intensive fleet with no durable pricing power through a downturn.
name: Carnival Corp Ltd.
one_liner: Largest cruise operator, moat 5/10, with a genuine TTM cash recovery ($2.23/share OE) — but at $26.82 it does not clear 15% (12.2% weighted, IV@15 $20.72); it clears at $20.72, and with a margin of safety only in the mid-teens given $24.71B of net debt.
